liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Viola Lee Blues** (1 review): The 21-minute version is described as pure energy [5]
- **Turn On Your Love Light** (1 review): Bobby sings the final verse, considered his best ever on that song [14]
- **Hurts Me Too** (1 other source): A speed change in this song was corrected during editing [1]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (1 other source): The That's It For The Other One suite was recorded but is unlistenable due to the battery problem [3]

## Setlist highlights

- **Politics**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]

## The recordings

- **gd68-03-03.aud.vernon.9374.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 6 songs; 59 min; rated 4.47/5 by 32 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording quality is not the best, but it documents an important show; Sound is not great but becomes tolerable over time; reviewer finds the band on fire [7][11]
- **gd68-03-03.aud.jools.19904.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 5 songs; 59 min; rated 3.67/5 by 15 [2]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is mediocre, though better than the tapes from 5/18/68 and 6/14/68 [5]
- **gd1968-03-03.aud.finney.5809.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 4 songs; 54 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [3]

## Around the show

- Called the Flatbed Truck show, a completely impromptu performance [5]
- Band drove a flatbed truck into the middle of Haight Street on a sunny day, closing the street [6]
- Reportedly lived in LA, taped Cream on Saturday night, then heard about the Dead's Sunday afternoon show [8]
- Someone blowing a whistle and noise in the background are audible; the stage banter is praised [9]
- The crowd can be heard going wild throughout the performance [10]
- Reviewer says the city closed the street for peace after a riot days earlier; the band set up without permits [12]
- Phil's book reportedly calls it the last great San Francisco experience before the band left town [12]
- A commune called Good Earth helped set up equipment for the Dead and other bands [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd68-03-03.aud.vernon.9374.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steve Brown; transferred by Lance Michel, Raoul Duke, and Matt Vernon; source: Audience [1]. Also: Taped by Steve Brown on an old Uher with a cheap microphone held up over the crowd; Source was a DAT with mono left channel, converted to mono and mastered to CD in Diamond Cut [1][6]
- **gd68-03-03.aud.jools.19904.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Julian (Jools) Elliott; source: Audience [2]. Also: Believed taped by Steve Brown, who later worked for the Dead [8]
- **gd1968-03-03.aud.finney.5809.sbeok.shnf**: source: DHH pre-FM [3]. Also: Master tape is incomplete because the tapers' batteries were running low [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LUV4MUSIC!: [Spotlight On What I Am Listening To: Grateful Dead - Haight Street, San Francisco, CA 1968-03-03 SBD? - LUV4MUSIC!](https://www.luv4music.org/2026/03/03/spotlight-on-what-i-am-listening-to-grateful-dead-haight-street-san-francisco-ca-1968-03-03-sbd/) [17]
